Devan Ramachandran, J.
The petitioner calls into question Exts.P12 and P16 orders of the learned Family Court, Thrissur.
2. Sri

.K.M.Muhammed Hussain - learned counsel for the petitioner, submitted that the orders of the learned Family Court, to allow the children to be taken out of the Court premises during the time when the respondent-father has been given their interim custody, is illegal and unlawful because,
the past experiences show that he has not taken care of them in a manner as a father should.

He,
therefore, prayed that Ext.P16 be set aside and the children be allowed to interact with the respondent only within the premises of the learned Family Court.

3. Before we move forward, we deem it necessary to record that we were rather surprised by the learned Family Court having allowed the children to be produced and exchanged at its premises in spite of our affirmative declaration in Indu v. Thomas 2025:KER:40839 OP(FC) 328/25 @ Manoj [2025(3) KHC 295].

entities.text: Indu v. Thomas 2025:KER:40839 OP(FC) 328/25 @ Manoj [2025(3) KHC 295]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We, therefore, called for a report from the learned Family Court which is now available.

The learned Court has informed us that 'in fact, there is nothing in conflict with the decision of the Hon'ble High Court in Indu v.
Thomas @ Manoj [2025(3) KHC 295]' (sic) since the impugned order was passed as per the request of both sides in this case.

4. Today, the learned counsel for the parties were ad idem that the children can be exchanged - for the purpose of interaction with their father, as ordered by the learned Family Court in Ext.P5 order dated 06.09.2024 - in front of the residential gate of the mother.

They also agreed that the children can be taken by the father at 10 A.M. and returned at 4 P.M.;
and that the latter can take them anywhere of his choice, however, ensuring that all their requirements, including food and other imperatives are fully taken care of.
5. In view of the afore consent, it becomes incumbent upon us only to dispose of the matter in terms of the same.
But before we do so, we deem it necessary to add one word regarding the report of the learned Family Court.

7. In Indu (supra), which was followed by a further judgment of ours reported as Plessy Francis v.
Dinto Mathews [2025 KHC Online 517] we have ordered that no Family Court shall ordinarily allow the exchange of children either in its premises or involving Police Stations.

entities.text:
Plessy Francis v.
Dinto Mathews [2025 KHC Online 517]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has also been rendered luculent that, it is only in exceptional circumstances and for reasons to be recorded, that the premises of the Court be used for such.

Therefore, if both the parties insisted on the exchange of children in its premises, then it was for the learned Family Court to have recorded so in its order in terms of the declarations in Indu (supra).
We do not find this in any of the orders impugned.

Binu Balachandran vs Arun Prakash on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40053662/
2
But we choose to leave it there.

Resultantly, we allow this Original Petition with the consent of both sides and modify Ext.P16 with the following directions.
a) The respondent-father will be allowed to be in interim 2025:KER:40839 OP(FC)
328/25 custody of the children from 10 A.M. till 4 P.M. every second Saturday and fourth Sunday.
The place of exchange for this shall be in front of the gate of the residence of the petitioner-mother at Pazhayannur.
b) The respondent-father will be entitled to take the children to any place of his choice; however, keeping in mind their requirements, safety and full well being.
c) This arrangement will continue until such time as it is modified by the learned Family Court in due course, or until GOP 642/2024 is disposed of, whichever is earlier.

Sd/-
DEVAN RAMACHANDRAN JUDGE Sd/-
